# VPN-nonVPN Dataset (ISCXVPN2016)

**Source:** Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity (CIC), University of New Brunswick (UNB)
**Download:** https://cicresearch.ca/CICDataset/ISCX-VPN-NonVPN-2016/ (registration required — name, email, institution, job title)
**Total size:** ~28 GB
**Formats:** Full packet captures (`.pcap`) + flow features (`.csv`, generated by ISCXFlowMeter)
**Local path:** `data/ISCXVPN2016/`

**Required citation:**
> G. Draper-Gil, A. H. Lashkari, M. S. I. Mamun, A. A. Ghorbani, "Characterization of Encrypted and VPN Traffic Using Time-Related Features," ICISSP 2016.

---

## Overview

To generate a representative dataset of real-world traffic, the authors defined a set of
tasks assuring the dataset is rich enough in diversity and quantity. They created accounts
for users **Alice** and **Bob** to use services like Skype, Facebook, etc.

Each traffic type was captured as a **regular session** and a **session over VPN**, giving a
total of **14 traffic categories** (e.g., VOIP, VPN-VOIP, P2P, VPN-P2P, …).

## Capture setup

- **Tools:** Wireshark and tcpdump, generating a total of **28 GB** of data.
- **VPN:** External VPN service provider, connected via **OpenVPN (UDP mode)**.
- **SFTP / FTPS:** External service provider, using **Filezilla** as the client.
- **Isolation:** During each capture, all unnecessary services and applications were closed —
  the only application running was the objective of the capture (e.g., Skype voice-call,
  SFTP file transfer, etc.).
- **Filtering:** A filter captured only packets whose source or destination IP was the local
  client (Alice or Bob), to facilitate labeling.
- **Flow features:** **ISCXFlowMeter** (written in Java) reads the `.pcap` files and creates
  the `.csv` file based on selected features.

The UNB ISCX Network Traffic (VPN-nonVPN) dataset consists of labeled network traffic,
including full packets in `pcap` format and `csv` flows generated by ISCXFlowMeter — both
publicly available for researchers.

## Traffic types and descriptions

- **Browsing** — HTTPS traffic generated by users while browsing or performing any task using
  a browser. For instance, capturing voice-calls via Hangouts also produced several browsing
  flows even though browsing was not the main activity.

- **Email** — Traffic generated using a **Thunderbird** client with Alice's and Bob's Gmail
  accounts. Clients were configured to deliver mail through **SMTP/S** and receive it using
  **POP3/SSL** in one client and **IMAP/SSL** in the other.

- **Chat** — Instant-messaging applications: **Facebook** and **Hangouts** via web browsers,
  **Skype**, and **IAM** and **ICQ** using the **pidgin** application.

- **Streaming** — Multimedia applications requiring a continuous, steady stream of data.
  Captured from **YouTube** (HTML5 and flash versions) and **Vimeo** using Chrome and Firefox.

- **File Transfer** — Applications whose main purpose is to send or receive files and
  documents: **Skype** file transfers, **FTP over SSH (SFTP)**, and **FTP over SSL (FTPS)**.

- **VoIP** — Voice over IP traffic from voice applications: voice calls using **Facebook**,
  **Hangouts**, and **Skype**.

- **P2P (TraP2P)** — File-sharing protocols like **Bittorrent**. Generated by downloading
  various `.torrent` files from a public repository and capturing sessions with **uTorrent**
  and **Transmission**.

## UNB ISCX Network Traffic Dataset content (summary)

| Traffic        | Content                                                        |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Web Browsing   | Firefox and Chrome                                            |
| Email          | SMTPS, POP3S and IMAPS                                        |
| Chat           | ICQ, AIM, Skype, Facebook and Hangouts                       |
| Streaming      | Vimeo and YouTube                                            |
| File Transfer  | Skype, FTPS and SFTP using Filezilla and an external service |
| VoIP           | Facebook, Skype and Hangouts voice calls (1h duration)       |
| P2P            | uTorrent and Transmission (Bittorrent)                       |
